title: Minecraft Cube Placer — Head Raycast Voxel Editor
description: The catalyst's voxel_editor mode raycasts from the player's head (XRCamera3D) to a grid cell, shows a ghost cube preview, and lets the player place or remove cubes with trigger press. This is the first and only catalyst skill at game start — a Minecraft-style building tool that teaches spatial reasoning before any algorithm modes unlock.
summary: Look with your head, trigger to place, double-trigger to remove. Can't build on the cell you're standing on. Only skill at start.
earned_from: Minecraft cube placer session — changed voxel mode from controller-ray to head-ray, added standing-cell guard, disabled mode persistence so only voxel_editor shows at start

nodes.label: Player picks up catalyst crystal
nodes.detail: Crystal shrinks into hand, absorbs permanently. Hand is free again. BecomingCatalyst auto-absorbs onto the XRController3D. Default mode: voxel_editor.

nodes.label: Voxel mode activates, finds XR nodes
nodes.detail: becoming_catalyst._activate_voxel_mode() creates a VoxelEditController child, then walks up from the controller to find XROrigin3D and its XRCamera3D child. These are cached for per-frame head raycasting.

nodes.label: Every frame: raycast from head into grid
nodes.detail: In _physics_process, _update_voxel_raycast() fires a ray from _xr_camera.global_position along -_xr_camera.basis.z. VoxelEditController.update_target_from_ray() does the physics query and computes target_cell (existing cube hit) and add_cell (adjacent empty cell).

nodes.label: Ghost cubes appear at target
nodes.detail: VoxelEditController shows a translucent green cube at add_cell (where new cube would go) and a red cube at target_cell (existing cube being aimed at). Both use top_level=true so they render at world scale regardless of catalyst's tiny absorbed scale.

nodes.label: Player presses trigger?
nodes.detail: Controller button_pressed signal fires 'trigger_click' or 'ax_button'. _on_controller_button routes to _handle_voxel_fire().

nodes.label: Double press? (< 350ms gap)
nodes.detail: _handle_voxel_fire() compares Time.get_ticks_msec() with _last_fire_time. If gap < DOUBLE_CLICK_MS (350), it's a double press.

nodes.label: Is add_cell on player's standing column?
nodes.detail: _is_player_standing_cell() converts XROrigin3D position (feet level) to grid coords via world_to_grid(), then compares XZ with the target add_cell. Blocks placement if they match.
nodes.code:
var player_grid = structure_component.world_to_grid(_xr_origin.global_position)
return player_grid.x == cell_x and player_grid.z == cell_z

nodes.label: Reject: short haptic buzz
nodes.detail: If player tries to build on their standing cell, a tiny haptic pulse (0.02s, amplitude 0.1) signals rejection. No cube placed.

nodes.label: Place cube at add_cell
nodes.detail: VoxelEditController.try_add() calls GridStructureComponent.stack_add(x, z) which increments the height column and rebuilds the MultiMesh. Haptic pulse confirms placement.

nodes.label: Remove cube at target_cell
nodes.detail: VoxelEditController.try_remove() calls GridStructureComponent.stack_remove(x, z) which decrements the height. No standing-cell guard on removal — you CAN remove the cube you're standing on.

nodes.label: Continue building
nodes.detail: Player keeps looking and placing. The ghost cube updates every frame. fire_cooldown (0.15s) prevents accidental rapid placement.
